summary: One unauthenticated GET `${baseUrl}/2026/schedule/conference.json` (live copy 824 009 bytes) with a 10 000 ms timeout. It sends no headers and has no ETag or TTL. name: Cache-then-network load with offline fallback (schedule-cache)
summary: On first use, load() reads the Ionic Storage key `schedule-cache` (the raw, unprocessed feed), processes it and emits it (first emission). It then GETs the network copy, sets data=null, reprocesses and emits again (second emission) before completing. If the network fails after the cache was served, it completes silently. If there is no cache and the network fails, it shows a toast 'Unable to load schedule, no offline cache available' (duration 3000, position 'top', icon 'exclamation') and the observable errors. processData writes `schedule-cache` on every run, including when fed the cache itself. app.component hides the Capacitor splash on the first emission or on error.
flet_hint: Data store with an async load(): read the cache JSON file from FLET_APP_STORAGE_CACHE → publish → fetch → write cache → publish; ft.SnackBar on total failure; a branded loading View until the first publish
gotchas: Two emissions on cold start (cache → network) for every query; pages re-render twice. A port that awaits a single result will show stale data until next launch, or never show cached data offline.
`processData` writes `schedule-cache` **every** time it runs (including when fed the cache itself).

[source-verified] load() returns a cold Observable: each subscription made while this.data is null starts its own storage read and its own 824 KB GET, with no in-flight dedupe. The port should share one task.
[source-verified] The second emission replaces every Session/Speaker object (this.data = null; processData(fresh)), so any view holding references from the first emission is stale.

name: In-memory memo and manual cache invalidation / refresh
summary: Processed data is memoised for the app's lifetime: load() returns of(this.data) synchronously once it is set. There is no TTL, no background refresh and no ETag. invalidateCache() runs `this.data = null; storage.remove('schedule-cache')`. It is called from pull-to-refresh on Sprints and Job Listings and from Dev Tools 'Invalidate Schedule Cache' (toast 'Schedule cache invalidated — pull to refresh'). Schedule pull-to-refresh shows a LoadingController 'Fetching latest schedule...' (10 s) and checks for a live update, but does NOT invalidate, so it re-serves memory.

name: Conference-timezone time labels and day bucketing
summary: timeStart/timeEnd = d.toLocaleTimeString([], {timeZone:'America/Los_Angeles', hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit'}).toLowerCase(), e.g. '9:00 am', '12:30 pm'. day = toLocaleDateString('en-us', {timeZone, weekday:'short'}), giving 'Wed'…'Sun'. The schedule day bucket is new Date(start + utcOffset(-7)*3600*1000).toISOString().split('T')[0], e.g. '2026-05-15'. Day labels use new Date(date+'T00:00:00.000-12:00') formatted as an en-us weekday in the conference TZ. parseTime('1:45 pm') returns minutes since midnight ('12 am'→0, '12 pm'→720). The lunch-rename hour comes from toLocaleTimeString([], {hour12:false}). startUtc/endUtc keep the raw ISO strings with the '-07:00' offset.

name: sha1 request signing for the PyCon API
summary: buildRequestAuthHeaders(method, url, body): apiKey = storage 'key'; secret = storage 'secret'; timestamp = Math.round(Date.now()/1000); baseString = [secret, timestamp, method, url, body].join(''). flet_hint: hashlib.sha1(f'{secret}{ts}{method}{path_qs}{body}'.encode()).hexdigest(); body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False); send content=body.encode() via httpx with the URL string you signed
gotchas: **Signature base string** has no separators and the body must be byte-identical to what is sent; timestamps are integer seconds (`Math.round`). URL in the signature includes the query string and `encodeURIComponent` encoding exactly as built.

[source-verified correction] The report says a missing key/secret produces a signature over "null…"; actually Array.join renders null/undefined as '' and Angular HttpHeaders rejects a null header value, so with no stored key the request most likely fails client-side — gate signed calls on login either way.

flet_hint: httpx via the signed client; outcome shown with a coloured ft.SnackBar(FLOATING) or a top ft.Banner
gotchas: **No local queue** — redemption requires connectivity; failures are only toasted.
Material snack bars are **bottom-anchored only**; `position: 'top'` ... has no SnackBar equivalent.

name: Attendee directory load
summary: /app/tabs/mask-violation, titled 'CoC Incident' ('mask violation' is a legacy name), is reached from the menu and Staff Tools (hasMaskViolation). On init it sends a signed GET /2026/api/v1/mask_violations/attendees/ (15 s) returning data [{access_code, full_name, nickname, badge_name, violations}], sorted by (full_name||nickname||badge_name).toLowerCase() with localeCompare. States: a dots spinner with 'Loading attendee directory…'; on error, warning-outline with 'Couldn't load attendee list.' and a small 'Retry' button. When there is no result and no query, an intro shows 'Capture an Incident' and two hints, the first starting 'Tap Start Scanner, point the camera at the attendee's badge QR code…' and the second 'Can't scan a badge? Search by name below and tap the attendee to record an incident the same way.'
flet_hint: Load in use_effect; ProgressRing or flet_spinkit ThreeBounce; keep the list in component state only (PII)
gotchas: The directory is loaded once per page instantiation (can be stale; counts updated locally after captures).
Name search is client-side over the full attendee list (size unknown; held in memory).

name: Attendee name search
summary: Searchbar 'Search attendee by name' (debounce 150, trimmed). The query is split on whitespace, and an attendee is kept only if EVERY term is a substring of the lower-cased full_name + ' ' + nickname + ' ' + badge_name. At most 25 rows. Each row: an h3 display name (600), 'Badge: <badge_name>' when it differs, '"<nickname>"' when it differs from the full name, and a trailing ion-badge '<n> incident(s)' colored danger (>2), warning (>0) or medium. When nothing matches: 'No attendees match "<query>"'. The list shows only when a query is set and the page is neither loading nor in error. Rows are disabled while capturing.
flet_hint: TextField + use_memo filter + ListView(ListTile with a trailing badge Container)
gotchas: Badge colour thresholds in the list (>2 danger, >0 warning) differ from the result card's (>2 danger, >1 warning).

name: Record an incident by name with notes (force)
summary: Tapping an attendee (ignored while capturing or when there is no access_code) opens an AlertController dialog. Header: 'Record CoC Incident'. subHeader: full_name || nickname || badge_name || 'this attendee'. Message lines: 'Badge: <badge_name>' (if it differs), 'Existing incidents: <violations ?? 0>', a blank line, and 'Add any context (location, what happened, witnesses). This is saved on the incident record.' (cssClass coc-confirm-alert, pre-line). It has one textarea input 'notes' (placeholder 'Notes (optional)', rows 4, maxlength 2000, autocapitalize sentences), backdropDismiss false, and buttons 'Cancel' and 'Record Incident'. Confirming sends a signed POST /2026/api/v1/mask_violations/capture/ with JSON {attendee_access_code, notes (only if non-empty after trimming), force: true} (5 s). The provider switches to POST whenever notes or force is present, so free text never lands in a URL.
flet_hint: AlertDialog(modal=True) with TextField(multiline, max_length=2000, capitalization=SENTENCES)
gotchas: `force` is sent **only** from the name-search path and is always `true` there; the scan path never sends it.
Capture errors only reset `capturing` (no toast — nothing visible happens).

name: Badge-scan incident capture (one request per detected frame)
summary: Start Scanner runs the permission check, sets scanning=true, and calls addListener without removing earlier listeners, then startScan. handleScan never removes or pauses the listener. Every barcodesScanned event clears the last-scan timeout and calls updateLastScan(raw.split(':')[0]), which sends a signed GET /2026/api/v1/mask_violations/capture/?attendee_access_code=<enc> (5 s, no notes, no force). The scan path has no capturing guard. Stop clears the card, removes the listeners and calls stopScan. The toggle button is never disabled.
flet_hint: flet-barcode-scanner on_detect with a per-code cooldown (e.g. 5 s) or a confirm step; a product/safety decision to make with the server team
gotchas: **CoC never pauses** (fires a capture per detected frame).
Holding a badge in view therefore fires repeated capture requests (server-side dedupe assumed; see open questions).
Verified in source: `updateLastScan` sets `capturing = true` but `handleScan` never checks it.

name: Incident result card
summary: A footer card driven by violationData.data. Color is danger when violations > 2, warning when > 1, otherwise success. Icon is alert-circle-outline when violations > 1, otherwise checkmark-circle-outline. It shows nickname || full_name in bold, 'Badge: <badge_name>', the email, and '<violations> incident(s) on record' with the number at 1.15rem/800. It auto-clears 5 s after the request was sent (the timer starts before the response arrives). The response's violations count updates the in-memory directory row and re-applies the filter.
flet_hint: Footer Card; start the auto-clear timer when the response arrives, not when the request is sent
gotchas: Auto-cleared **5 s after the request was sent** (timer starts before the response).
The 5 s auto-clear can hide a slow response before it renders.
